other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 1555, Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act of 2025

summary: The Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act of 2025 increases the maximum loan limits available to certain small domestic manufacturing businesses under specific Small Business Administration and Small Business Investment Act loan programs. It also requires the Small Business Administration Inspector General to analyze default rates and risks from these increased limits within two years, and mandates annual reports from the Small Business Administration on job creation and retention linked to these larger loans over a five-year period.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible small businesses whose primary operations fall under specific North American Industrial Classification System sectors and whose production facilities are entirely in the United States may qualify for larger federal loan amounts up to $10,000,000.

The Small Business Administration Inspector General and Administrator must conduct mandated risk analyses, track default rates, and submit multiple reports to congressional committees over a period of up to 4 years.

key_provisions: Defines a 'small manufacturer' as a small business whose primary business is classified in sector 31, 32, or 33 of the North American Industrial Classification System and whose production facilities are all located in the United States.

Increases Small Business Act section 7(a) loan guaranty limits for eligible small manufacturers, raising certain loan and gross loan thresholds up to $7,500,000, $9,000,000, or $10,000,000 depending on the specific subsection and use.
Increases the maximum loan amount under section 502(2)(A)(iii) of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 from $5,500,000 to $10,000,000 for small manufacturers.

Requires the Inspector General of the Small Business Administration to conduct an analysis within 2 years regarding default rates, early default rates, and potential financial risks to government loan programs resulting from the higher loan limits.

Requires the Administrator of the Small Business Administration to submit annual reports for the year of enactment and the next 4 years to congressional committees detailing data on larger loans given to small manufacturers, including metrics on job creation, job retention, and cost-per-job ratios.
missing_information: Total funding appropriations or exact budgetary costs are not specified in the text.
The total number of small manufacturers expected to apply for or receive these increased loans is not estimated.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act of 2025 increases the maximum loan limits available to certain small domestic manufacturing businesses under specific Small Business Administration and Small Business Investment Act loan programs. It also requires the Small Business Administration Inspector General to analyze default rates and risks from these increased limits within two years, and mandates annual reports from the Small Business Administration on job creation and retention linked to these larger loans over a five-year period.
summary_detail.significance: The bill adjusts federal financing rules to potentially allow certain domestic manufacturing businesses to access larger government-backed loans. Because it changes loan ceilings and mandates oversight reporting, its significance is evaluated as limited to moderate depending on how many small manufacturers utilize the higher limits.
